selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: Where did the traveller arrive in this passage?
questions.answer: He came to the school of Imam-i Rabbani, Ahmad Faruqi, who is described as the Renewer of the Second Millenium.

questions.question: What does this teach about priorities in religion?
questions.answer: It teaches that strong and clear belief comes before miraculous or emotional experiences.

questions.question: What did the Imam say about his relation to that hoped-for person?
questions.answer: He said he wished to be that person and that perhaps he was.

questions.question: What role does reflective thinking play in this section?
questions.answer: It is treated as a high form of worship when it is focused on faith.

questions.question: In the passage, how is the silent remembrance of the Naqshbandi way understood?
questions.answer: It is presented as a form of that excellent reflective worship.

questions.question: According to the traveller, how valuable is even the smallest increase in faith?
questions.answer: He sees it as more precious than very large amounts of other spiritual gains.

questions.question: Why are those foundations of belief so important in the passage?
questions.answer: They are presented as the key and basis for everlasting happiness, endless life, and Paradise.

questions.question: What response does he urge in the face of these attacks?
questions.answer: He urges believers to move from secondhand faith to faith confirmed by realization.

questions.question: What door did he say they would knock on?
questions.answer: He said they would knock on the door of the Lord’s sustenance for living creatures.

questions.question: Which divine name is especially highlighted at the moment the gate opens?
questions.answer: Allah is highlighted as the Opener.

questions.question: Which Islamic scholar’s school appears in the passage?
questions.answer: The school of Imam-i Rabbani, Ahmad Faruqi, appears in the passage.

questions.question: How does the text compare certainty in belief with supernatural-seeming experiences?
questions.answer: It says certainty in belief is better than many miracles and mystical visions.

questions.question: What kind of person had earlier great figures expected to appear?
questions.answer: They expected a scholar who would prove the truths of Islam and faith with reason and clear evidence.

questions.question: According to the lesson, what place do faith and tawhid hold in the life of a person?
questions.answer: They are the basis and life-source of all true human perfection.

questions.question: What practice is connected to the Hadith about an hour of thought?
questions.answer: Serious reflection on the truths of faith is connected to it.

questions.question: What did the traveller say about a very small increase in faith?
questions.answer: He said it is worth more than huge amounts of other spiritual attainments.

questions.question: Which outside group is portrayed as opposing faith and the Qur’an?
questions.answer: European philosophers are portrayed that way.

questions.question: What kind of faith is not enough according to the traveller?
questions.answer: Faith that is merely imitated from others is not enough.

questions.question: Why does the traveller mention the number thirty-three?
questions.answer: It matches the number of litanies recited after the prescribed prayer.

questions.question: What does the traveller call the next stage he wants to see?
questions.answer: He calls it the third stopping-place in that world of instruction.

questions.question: Who was teaching when the traveller entered the school?
questions.answer: Imam-i Rabbani was teaching.

questions.question: What did he do after entering the school?
questions.answer: He listened to the Imam’s lesson.

questions.question: How does the explanatory note shift attention away from one person?
questions.answer: It directs attention to a body of writings as the true answer to that expectation.

questions.question: How does the footnote reinterpret the prediction?
questions.answer: It says the prediction truly pointed to the Risale-i Nur itself.
